questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Shall have / you bring / your note-book / tomorrow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of **"Shall have"** at the beginning of the question.
 
• In standard English, the correct form should be** "Shall you have"** or** "Will you bring".**
 
• The phrase **"Shall have" **is not typically used to form a question in this context.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Sentence: *"Shall you bring your note-book tomorrow?"***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) "tomorrow" **– This part of the sentence is correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2) "your note-book"** – This part of the sentence is correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4) "you bring"** – This part of the sentence is correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.

questions.question: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.

options.text: If you had work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you have work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you worked hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The second option correctly uses the future tense by stating, **"If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."**
 
• It properly combines the present simple tense **"work"** with the** future simple tense "will achieve."**
 
• This structure follows the** first conditional format**, which is used for real or possible situations in the future.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "If you had work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect because "had work" is not grammatically correct; it should be "had worked" for past perfect tense, but then it doesn't match with "will achieve."
 
• **Option 3: "If you have work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect because "have work" is not correct; it should be "have worked," but the present perfect tense with "will achieve" is not the correct match in this conditional sentence structure.
 
• **Option 4: "If you worked hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect as it mixes past simple tense "worked" with future simple tense "will achieve," which typically demands a different conditional format (second conditional).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

He has ___________ vision because of his illness.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"blurred"** is the most appropriate word to describe vision that is affected by an illness. It accurately conveys the idea of unclear or indistinct vision, which is a common symptom of various illnesses.
 
• The other options, such as** "obscured," "unfocused," and "faded," **do not precisely capture the typical way of describing vision problems due to illness.
 
• "Blurred vision" is a commonly used medical term that specifically refers to the loss of sharpness of vision and the inability to see fine details.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"He has **blurred** vision because of his illness."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "obscured"** – This word suggests that something is blocking the vision, but it doesn't specifically describe the quality of the vision itself.
 
• **Option 3: "unfocused"** – This term implies that the vision is not sharp, but it is less commonly used in the context of vision problems due to illness.
 
• **Option 4: "faded"** – This word suggests a loss of color or brightness, which is not typically how vision problems are described.
